title: Phase 4 · Stage 13: The monthly report
summary: Build the librarian's report with GroupBy, joins across books, loans and members, and aggregates.

steps.title: Grouping
body: The library board wants a monthly report: how the collection breaks down by genre, who borrows most, what is overdue and how much is owed. Every one of those is a **group** or a **join**.
`GroupBy` sorts items into buckets by a key. Each group *is* a sequence of its items, with a `Key`:
Only keys that occur get a group: a genre with no books simply does not appear.
One more helper before the report: English plurals. `Plural(2, "title")` is fine, but *copy* becomes *copies*, so give `Plural` an optional third parameter: `Plural(n, "copy", "copies")`.

linq.setup: record Book(string Title, string Genre, int Copies);
linq.source: new[] { new Book("Hobbit", "Fiction", 3), new Book("Dune", "Science", 1), new Book("LOTR", "Fiction", 2), new Book("Cosmos", "Science", 2), new Book("Emma", "General", 1) }

code: foreach (var g in books.GroupBy(b => b.Item2).OrderBy(g => g.Key))
steps.explain: Two buckets. Notice the grammar on the second line: that is exactly why the report uses a `Plural` helper.

Genres appear in enum order, only when they have books. With no books the genre section is the single line `  (no books)`.
4. `help` gains `report` before `stats`: `..., fines, pay, report, stats, fine, help, quit`.

require.message: Plural has an optional plural form

hints: Build the report as a `List<string>` and `string.Join("\n", output)` at the end. The first two lines and `By genre:` go in the collection initializer.
`books.GroupBy(b => b.Genre).OrderBy(g => g.Key)` gives one group per genre in enum order; each group has `Count()` and `Sum(...)` like any sequence.
The on-loan count for a group is `g.Sum(b => b.TotalCopies - b.AvailableCopies)`; add every group line with `output.AddRange(...)`.

steps.title: Joins and aggregates
body: A loan only stores ids: `Isbn` and `MemberId`. To print *The Hobbit -> Ada Lovelace*, the report has to **join** loans to books and members on those keys. Query syntax reads almost like the sentence:
join book in library.Books on loan.Isbn equals book.Isbn
join member in library.Members on loan.MemberId equals member.Id
`join` builds a lookup on one side, so it is fast even for big lists (no loop inside a loop). `let` names a value once so `orderby` and `select` can share it.
**Aggregate** folds a sequence into one value with your own rule. `Sum` only knows numbers, but `Money` has a `+`:

steps.prompt: Match each part of the report to the LINQ that builds it.
pairs: how many loans each member has had
the loan's title and the borrower's name
most loans first, ties by name
steps.explain: Grouping counts, joining names, ordering ranks, `Take` trims and `Aggregate` totals.

steps.prompt: Which query gives *how many copies each genre has*?
steps.explain: Group by the key, then aggregate each group. The last option only answers for one genre.

steps.title: The report, part 2: people and money
prompt: `Library` exposes `IReadOnlyDictionary<int, Money> Balances`. The report gains three sections after the genres:
The Hobbit -> Grace Hopper, 6 days late
- **Top borrowers**: everyone's loans **ever** (returned or not), most first, ties by name (ordinal), at most 3, numbered. None: `  (no loans yet)`.
- **Overdue**: active loans past their due date, joined to their book and member, most days late first, then by title. None: `  (nothing overdue)`.
- **Fines owed**: the total of all balances (use `Aggregate`) and how many members owe more than zero. When nobody owes anything: `Fines owed: nothing`.

require.message: Joins loans to books or members
Keeps the top three with Take(3)

hints: Top borrowers: join loans to members (`library.Loans.Join(library.Members, l => l.MemberId, m => m.Id, (l, m) => m)`), group by name, order by count descending then name, `Take(3)`. `Select((g, i) => ...)` gives you the position for the number.
Overdue: the query from the card, wrapped in `( ... ).ToList()` so you can check whether it is empty.
`Money owed = library.Balances.Values.Aggregate(Money.Zero, (sum, balance) => sum + balance);` and count the members with `Count(balance => balance != Money.Zero)`.
